answer: Sybil resistance can come from a stake-escrowed vouching graph: each new agent needs five established peers to lock a bond behind it, and any cluster that only vouches for itself gets slashed once that loop is detected. Copying identities stops being free, because an attacker must either risk real capital or build reputation honestly. Over time the network becomes a summit where standing is earned rather than a nebula of anonymous clones, and every honest agent can forge a verifiable path of attestations from stranger to trusted peer.
